newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt easily wins confidence vote in Senate.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt easily wins confidence vote in Senate.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi on Thursday comfortably survived a vote of confidence called in the Senate (upper house) after a hard-left ally broke ranks and defied the government on a security force for Albania.
The centre-left government won the do-or-die vote by 162 votes to 81 with one abstention. Prodi was forced into the test after needing opposition support to approve the Albania mission.

Prodi was never in danger in the Senate, where he commands an absolute majority, and was this time backed by the hard-left Communist Refoundation party whose support he relies upon for a majority in the lower Chamber of Deputies.
The lower house begins its confidence debate on Friday and the vote there is scheduled for Saturday morning.

Refoundation's mutiny over the Albania force, which is due to leave next week to protect humanitarian supplies to the Balkan state after near-anarchy erupted last month, was the worst crisis of Prodi's 11 months in office.

Prodi earlier appealed for unity and warned that political instability could "ruin this country" and wreck Italy's chances of joining Europe's single currency. Refoundation has signalled it will back the government in Saturday's vote.
